gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per watt-hour of the 5 kWh units at this week's prices: the Anker SOLIX S5000 at $2,499.99 is $0.50 per rated Wh (and $0.51 per Wh that pv magazine's reviewer saw delivered), against $0.69 for the sold-out Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and $0.43 for the pre-order Pecron F5000LFP.
standout_why: Compared against offgridcurrent.com (whole-home page, opened), powerstations.reviews (opened, first 100,000 characters), thesolarlab.com (opened) and the Popular Mechanics and Car and Driver citations as ChatGPT quoted them (both sites blocked my fetch). offgridcurrent already gives the idle watts (Jackery 50 W, Anker 8.8 W), weights and modelled runtimes (35 h vs 49 h at 79 W; 22 h vs 27 h at 150 W), but no prices and no $/Wh. powerstations.reviews has a Price per Wh column and a Wh-per-lb sort, but in the part I read it lists only the Jackery and Pecron, not the S5000 or the Titan 5000 units. thesolarlab has only the Jackery, with no price or measured figures. ChatGPT's own answer prices the S5000 at $3,599.99 and already quotes the Popular Mechanics figure of nearly 4,900 Wh delivered. So the parts are scattered across rivals; what none has is the S5000's $/Wh at $2,499.99 next to the others, or idle draw expressed as a share of the battery per day.
decides: It reverses ChatGPT's price logic. ChatGPT picked the Jackery at $3,499 over the Anker at $3,599.99; at $2,499.99 the S5000 is $999 cheaper, 37.5 lb lighter and loses about 211 Wh a day to idle against about 1,200 Wh for the Jackery, which the pages I read show as sold out. The Jackery keeps only its 7,200 W output case (large 240 V loads). Two caveats on the S5000 as the pick: Dealectric's 11-27 store read says orders ship in 15-16 weeks, and the Pecron F5000LFP is cheaper per Wh ($0.43) with 7,200 W, but it is a pre-order whose ship date I could not read.

findings.label: Price per rated Wh
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: $2,499.99 / 5,024 Wh = $0.498. pv magazine gives $2,499.99 as the launch price and $3,599.99 as MSRP; backuppowerhub.com/?p=9229 (read 2026-11-27) shows $2,499.99 as its lowest tracked price dated Nov 27, though its Nov 10 check lists $2,599.99. Anker's own page showed no price in my fetch; the brief's 11-27 store read also says $2,499.99. Capacity from https://www.ankersolix.com/s5000.

findings.label: Price per Wh delivered (reviewer discharge)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha)
findings.note: $2,499.99 / 4,870 Wh = $0.513. Andrew Riha: the app reported 4.87 kWh delivered on a full discharge, 97% of nameplate (4,870 / 5,024 = 96.9%). This is app-reported; he did not meter the output.

findings.label: Wh per lb
findings.note: 5,024 Wh / 97 lb = 51.8. Both figures are Anker's.

findings.label: Energy the unit spends on itself per 24 h, 120 V output on
findings.value: 211 Wh per day, 4.2% of the battery
findings.note: 8.8 W idle (Anker) x 24 h = 211 Wh; 211 / 5,024 = 4.2%. Cross-check: Andrew Riha (pv magazine USA) saw 5% state of charge lost in 24 h with the 120 V output on and nothing connected, about 10 W by his estimate. Anker's rated standby of 512 h at 120 V works out to 5,024 / 512 = 9.8 W.

findings.label: Idle loss per 24 h with 240 V output on
findings.value: about 354 Wh per day, 7% of the battery
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha)
findings.note: Anker-rated standby of 341 h at 240 V, quoted by pv magazine: 5,024 Wh / 341 h = 14.7 W; x 24 h = 354 Wh. backuppowerhub.com/?p=9229 quotes Anker's spec sheet at 13.7 W with 240 V on (329 Wh per day). Riha did not measure 240 V idle.

findings.label: Average load carried in a real outage
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha)
findings.note: Riha ran a large refrigerator plus phones and small devices through a utility shutoff. 82% x 5,024 Wh = 4,120 Wh; 4,120 / 61.5 h = 67 W drawn from the battery, idle draw included.

findings.label: Refill from a 120 V wall outlet, and wall energy per full charge
findings.value: 3 h 39 min; 6.24 kWh from the wall; 78% round trip
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha)
findings.note: Riha at the 1,800 W setting: about 1.79 kW for 2 h 49 min, then about 1.43 kW for 50 min; 2:49 + 0:50 = 3:39. 4.87 kWh out / 6.24 kWh in = 78%. Anker's page says 1,800 W max at 120 V (over 3 hours) and 4,500 W at 240 V with 0-100% in 99 minutes.

findings.label: Price per kWh cycled over rated life
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Review: 5kWh of 240V Home Backup in a 97 lb Package (Backup Power Hub)
findings.note: $2,499.99 / (5.024 kWh x 6,000 cycles) = $0.083. Backup Power Hub quotes Anker at 6,000 cycles to 80% and 10,000 to 60%; Anker's page states the 10,000-to-60% figure. This is a floor: it ignores capacity fade and conversion loss, so the real cost per kWh is higher.

findings.label: Price per rated Wh
findings.source_title: Power station spec database: all 129 models, CSV (powerstations.reviews)
findings.note: $3,499 / 5,040 Wh = $0.694. The database shows the maker price as $3,499, sold out; backuppowerhub.com/?p=9229 also shows $3,499 sold out and $694 per kWh. jackery.com returned HTTP 429 and 403 to me, so this is not the maker's page.

findings.label: Wh per lb
findings.note: 5,040 Wh / 134.5 lb = 37.5. OffGrid Current (updated 2026-11-23) lists both figures; powerstations.reviews has the same weight. It is 134.5 - 97 = 37.5 lb heavier than the S5000.

findings.label: Energy the unit spends on itself per 24 h
findings.value: 1,200 Wh per day, 23.8% of the battery
findings.note: 50 W standby as OffGrid Current lists it x 24 h = 1,200 Wh; 1,200 / 5,040 = 23.8%. That is 989 Wh a day more than the S5000's 211 Wh. OffGrid Current says it has not tested the units; I could not confirm the 50 W on Jackery's page or manual.

findings.label: Price per rated Wh and Wh per lb
findings.source_title: Power station spec database: all 129 models, CSV (powerstations.reviews)
findings.note: $2,199 / 5,120 Wh = $0.429; 5,120 Wh / 123.9 lb = 41.3. The database lists 5,120 Wh, 7,200 W, 123.9 lb and a maker price of $2,199 against $2,999. pecron.com returned HTTP 429 and 403 to me, so the price and pre-order status are not from the maker's page.

findings.label: Wh per lb
findings.note: 5,017.6 Wh / 121.3 lb (55 kg) = 41.4. EcoFlow's spec page also gives 7,200 W at 120/240 V and 1,800 W AC input on the standard cord. This is the Canadian page; the US store returned HTTP 429 and 403.

findings.label: What the rivals already state
findings.value: Runtime at 79 W: 35 h Jackery, 49 h Anker; at 150 W: 22 h and 27 h
findings.note: OffGrid Current's model: 85% AC efficiency plus each maker's idle draw; not tested. A page built on this angle should not lead with hours-of-runtime, because this cited rival already has them.

Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus price, stock status, idle draw and 120 V recharge time from Jackery's page or manual: jackery.com returned HTTP 429 twice and 403 to the store tool.
Pecron F5000LFP price, ship date, idle draw and AC input from pecron.com: HTTP 429 and 403. Search snippets showed batch dates that have already passed.
OUKITEL ABEARL P5000 price, weight and idle draw: oukitel.com returned HTTP 403 and I opened no other page for it, so it has no figures here.

A reviewer-measured usable Wh for the Jackery 5000 Plus, Pecron F5000LFP or any Titan 5000, needed for $ per delivered Wh on every row: none of the pages I opened has one.
